title: Panel Beater Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual, Fortnightly, and After-Tax Pay
description: Understand panel beater salary calculations: convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay. Includes award rates, casual loading, super, and Medicare levy.
salarySummary: A panel beater's salary depends on the applicable award rate; for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a panel beater in Australia?
faqs.a: Panel beaters are typically covered by the Vehicle Manufacturing, Repair, Services and Retail Award 2020. Minimum rates vary by classification and experience. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides provide the exact rates. As a floor, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for award/agreement-free employees, but award rates are usually higher.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly panel beater rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes no overtime, penalty rates, or unpaid leave.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the panel beater salary figure?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual salary is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding a Panel Beater Salary

If you're a panel beater or considering the trade, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay is essential. A **panel beater salary** is typically set by the *Vehicle Manufacturing, Repair, Services and Retail Award 2020*, but many employers offer above-award rates. This guide explains the conversion process using the standard 38-hour week, and covers tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### Hourly to Annual: The Basic Formula

The standard calculation for full-time employees is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a panel beater working 38 hours per week, that's:

- $30/hour → $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year
- $35/hour → $35 × 38 × 52 = $72,280 per year
- $40/hour → $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 per year

This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work more than 38 hours, overtime rates (usually time-and-a-half or double time) would apply, but those are not included in this basic estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay:

**Fortnightly gross = hourly rate × 38 × 2**

Using the examples above:

- $30/hour → $30 × 76 = $2,280 per fortnight
- $35/hour → $35 × 76 = $2,660 per fortnight
- $40/hour → $40 × 76 = $3,040 per fortnight

Your actual bank deposit will be less after tax and the Medicare levy are withheld.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). This is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, panel beaters are almost always covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database with exact classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman also provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

If you are a casual panel beater, you are entitled to a **casual loading** of 25% on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the award rate is $28 per hour, a casual would receive $35 per hour. Our [timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross **panel beater salary**, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|----------------|-------------------|
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15¢ for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 plus 30¢ for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 plus 37¢ for each $1 over $135,000 |
| $190,001+ | $51,370 plus 45¢ for each $1 over $190,000 |

Additionally, the **Medicare levy** is generally 2% of your taxable income. There are reductions for low-income earners (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as a guide). For example, a panel beater earning $70,000 per year would pay:

- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($70,000 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $7,500 = $11,520
- Medicare levy: 2% × $70,000 = $1,400
- Total deductions: $12,920
- Net annual pay: $70,000 – $12,920 = $57,080

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed calculation.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **superannuation guarantee** contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual **panel beater salary** is $70,000, your employer adds $8,400 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Comparing Panel Beater Pay to Averages

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports **Average Weekly Earnings** for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to about $108,352 per year. Many panel beaters earn below this average, but experienced tradespeople in high-demand areas can exceed it. The ABS figure includes all industries; specific trade data may differ.

### Using Our Tools

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page lets you enter any hourly rate and instantly see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. The [timesheet](/) is designed for casual and permanent employees alike. Remember to check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for the exact award covering your role.

### Key Takeaways

- A **panel beater salary** is usually based on an award rate, not the National Minimum Wage.
- Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52 for full-time.
- Fortnightly gross = hourly rate × 76.
- Casual employees get a 25% loading on top.
- Tax and Medicare levy reduce your take-home pay.
- Super is paid on top at 12%.
- Always refer to the Fair Work Commission or Fair Work Ombudsman for official rates.

For a personalised estimate, use our [reference tables](/data) or [about the timesheet](/about) to understand how we calculate these figures.
